structure.description: FCC gamma matrix with spherical L12 gamma-prime precipitates

evidence_units.mechanism: Low matrix stacking-fault energy and high precipitate anti-phase-boundary energy impede deformation.

outcome.direction: higher than reported high-entropy alloys across the tested temperatures

limitations: Strength remains below CMSX-4 and CMSX-10.
evidence_spans: After the solution and aging heat-treatments, the microstructure consists of γ matrix and dispersed γ′ precipitates is shown in Fig. 2(a) .
The γ′ precipitates appears to be spherical with an average size of 290 nm and 69 vol% measured by image analysis.
The precipitation strengthening has allowed HESA to possess higher tensile yield strengths than those of CoCrFeMnNi throughout the temperatures.
Furthermore, the tensile yield strengths of HESA are the highest among reported high entropy alloys.

material.name: high entropy superalloy (HESA)
material.initial_state: solution and aging heat-treated gamma/gamma-prime microstructure

intervention.description: Expose HESA to 159 MPa at 750, 850, and 982 °C

evidence_units.mechanism: Positive gamma/gamma-prime misfit promotes rafting during creep; the response is dominated by tertiary creep.
limitations: The 982 °C response has no obvious primary creep and extensive tertiary creep.
evidence_spans: The creep rupture life of HESA at 982 °C is about 114 h, which is similar to those of several first-generation Ni-based superalloys under similar test conditions, e.g., the creep life of NX-188 DS under 982 °C/138 MPa test is 58 h [35] , and that of Rene′ 80 under 982 °C/145 MPa test is 118 h [36] .
Positive misfit between FCC matrix and precipitate has yielded parallel raft microstructure during creep at 982 °C, and the creep curves of HESA were dominated by tertiary creep behavior.
